transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ethan Brown (Redwood SE); Rita Kapoor (CTO, Crescent Labs); Samir Desai (Lead ML Eng); Lena Park (Platform Ops)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on integration surface area: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy pattern, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency and data residency reasons. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security pack, SDK examples, and schedule technical benchmark.

Topics:
- Current stack and traffic patterns
- Integration approach (direct SDK vs gateway/proxy)
- LangChain / LlamaIndex compatibility and examples
- Rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant isolation
- Observability hooks and tracing/troubleshooting
- Security (SOC2, KMS, VPC)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Ethan our SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Rita (Crescent): Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Rita, CTO. We have Samir and Lena on as well. Running a pretty full day so we'll keep this tight.
[00:12] Maya: Great, appreciate it. High level — want to understand your stack, what you're trying to build with LLMs, and then integration questions, especially around LangChain/LlamaIndex and gateway patterns.
[00:22] Samir: Sure. We're Crescent Labs, building a data-to-text insights product. Currently prototype on-host with OpenAI but latency and cost are climbing. We're exploring Redwood for serving — hosted to move fast, maybe dedicated later for predictability.
[00:34] Ethan (Redwood SE): Good context — can you share typical QPS, average prompt length, and whether you use streaming? Those drive kernel and batching choices.
[00:42] Samir: Right now 15 req/s at peak, average prompt ~350 tokens, sometimes up to 1k for long reports. We use streaming in our UI.
[00:53] Lena (Platform Ops): Also important: data residency — some clients require EU-only. And we need audit logs and KMS integration for keys.
[01:03] Maya: Makes sense. On residency, Redwood Hosted has regions and we can pin to EU-hosted capacity; Dedicated gives you isolation and VPC/private options. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Dedicated and Private.
[01:20] Rita: Can you explain the integration surface — what's the recommended route? We currently use LangChain in a few services and LlamaIndex in another.
[01:28] Ethan: Sure. Two common patterns: 1) Direct SDK calls from your app/services to Redwood's REST/SDK — quick and simple. 2) Gateway/proxy pattern — you put an internal gateway that handles auth, rate limiting, caching, and mapping LLM calls; that gateway talks to Redwood. Gateway helps unify different LLM backends and add observability.
[01:46] Samir: We're leaning gateway because we already route to multiple providers and want to swap models without code changes. Any SDKs for LangChain/LlamaIndex?
[01:55] Ethan: Yes — we've got first-class SDKs and adapter recipes. For LangChain, the Redwood model wrapper is a drop-in LLM class; for LlamaIndex we have small glue code examples. We'll share notebooks. Note: some of the community names get spelled weird in transcripts, like Llam-a index, but the libs are compatible.
[02:12] Maya: Also discussion about batching — Redwood's SDK supports auto-batching when using the hosted runtime; in Dedicated you can tune batching and quantization profiles.
[02:22] Lena: About rate limits: We need per-tenant quotas and burst handling. Can Redwood enforce per-API-key quotas?
[02:29] Ethan: Yes, both at the control plane and at request router. You can configure per-api-key quotas and rate limits, plus shared rate policies. For Dedicated, you can enforce stricter isolation and egress controls. We also support graceful degradation — fallback model variants when capacity pressure.
[02:45] Rita: Observability — we need traceability down to token latency and cost per request. What hooks exist?
[02:52] Ethan: Redwood Console has per-route token usage, latency breakdowns, and spans for each request. You can push traces to Jaeger/OTLP and export metrics to Prometheus. We also emit structured events for beginning/end of request, KV cache hits, and batching decisions.
[03:06] Samir: Is there an SDK-level hook so our gateway can annotate traces?
[03:10] Ethan: Yep — SDK supports context propagation headers and you can attach metadata (user ids, request ids). We'll include sample middleware for Node/Python to pass trace IDs through.
[03:20] Lena: For gateway pattern, do you recommend we handle caching or use Redwood's prefix/KV caching?
[03:27] Ethan: Preface caching: Redwood offers automatic prefix and KV cache to reduce token compute. For gateway-level caching you can add a layer for deduping identical prompts across tenants. In Dedicated/Private, you often combine both — gateway caches short-term responses; Redwood cache manages KV for the model's KV cache.
[03:43] Rita: Security — SOC2 scope and do you provide audit logs for request payloads? Also, can we redact sensitive fields?
[03:50] Maya: We provide audit logs, request/response metadata; payload retention is configurable. For Hosted, default retention is short but enterprise contracts allow control. Dedicated/Private gives you full control — you can disable logging of request bodies and integrate with your SIEM. KMS integration available for key rotation.
[04:06] Samir: When you say disable logging of request bodies, do you still provide fidelity for debugging? We need ability to replay a request under controlled conditions.
[04:14] Ethan: You can configure a sandbox where selected requests are logged and encrypted with customer KMS. There's also replay tooling in the Console that works with consented logs.
[04:23] Rita: About model rollouts: can you do canaries/A-B tests?
[04:27] Maya: Yes — rollouts are per-route with traffic splits, automatic fallback, and metrics-based health checks. Good for staged deployments.
[04:35] Samir: Back to LangChain — do you support streaming with LangChain integrations?
[04:39] Ethan: We support streaming at the SDK layer; LangChain chains that support streaming should work with our wrapper. We'll provide an example app. Note that streaming behavior interacts with batching heuristics.
[04:50] Lena: Any constraints on embedding APIs? We use vector DBs (Pinecone). Does Redwood provide embeddings or do we route to external embedders?
[04:58] Ethan: Redwood offers embeddings endpoints; you can also call external embedders. For integration with Pinecone, we have sample connector patterns. Many customers do: generate embeddings via Redwood and upsert to Pinecone.
[05:10] Rita: What's the recommended approach for multi-region traffic? We have EU clients and US clients.
[05:15] Maya: Smart routing can route by region or by latency policy; you can pin a route to an EU-only model. For Dedicated, you can deploy regional pools.
[05:23] Samir: Performance: we need 99th pct latency under 250ms for short prompts — is that realistic?
[05:29] Ethan: For short prompts on Dedicated with optimized kernels, yes. Hosted also achieves low latency on smaller models; it depends on model size and sequence length. We'll propose a benchmark run.
[05:39] Rita: How is authentication from our gateway? API keys or mTLS?
[05:44] Ethan: API keys for most flows, with optional mTLS and private links for Dedicated/Private. SSO for Console access and SAML/SCIM for user management.
[05:53] Lena: About costs — can we get unit economics: tokens per second, GPU hours, etc., so we can compare hosted vs dedicated?
[06:00] Maya: We'll share a sample cost model. Dedicated uses committed capacity and yields predictability; hosted is pay-as-you-go. Optimize via batching, KV caching, and quantization suggestions.
[06:12] Samir: Any gotchas when integrating with LlamaIndex — memory and state management?
[06:18] Ethan: LlamaIndex tends to create more context management; be mindful of index chunk sizes and embedding use. We saw customers stash index calls separately and use the gateway to orchestrate retrieval + generation. We'll include a reference pattern.
[06:30] Rita: For the prototype, we'd like an SE-run benchmark: 1) run our 50 top prompts, 2) measure latency/cost on hosted vs dedicated variant, 3) show LangChain streaming example.
[06:40] Ethan: Happy to run that. We'll need a test corpus, API keys, and an agreed prompt set.
[06:46] Lena: We also need to confirm data residency and SOC2 docs before we run any real client data through.
[06:52] Maya: We'll share the security pack and redact controls first.
[06:55] Samir: Any limitations on token length for streaming or chunking?
[06:59] Ethan: Models have max context lengths; Redwood supports long-context models and chunking helpers. For streaming, we stream as tokens are produced; batching heuristics may increase latency slightly for very low qps.
[07:12] Rita: On quotas, if a tenant exceeds quota, can we surface friendly errors?
[07:17] Ethan: Yes, the gateway can translate Redwood 429s into tenant-specific messages, and we support webhooks for quota events.
[07:24] Samir: About observability — do you ship sample Grafana dashboards?
[07:28] Ethan: Yes, Console has built-in dashboards; we also provide Grafana/Prometheus templates.
[07:33] Maya: Quick recap of what we'll send: pricing grid for hosted/dedicated/private, security pack, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and we'll schedule the SE benchmark. Any other questions?
[07:43] Rita: Timeline wise we have procurement in 3-4 weeks; ideally a pilot next month.
[07:48] Maya: Sounds good. We'll aim to have materials by Monday and propose benchmark slots next week.
[07:53] Samir: One more minor thing — do you support per-route model pinning for experiments?
[07:57] Ethan: Yes — route config allows model pinning and traffic splits.
[08:02] (cross-talk, agreement on next steps)
[08:10] Maya: Okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and action items.

End of transcript.
